```{r}
#Clear everything out and start fresh
rm(list=ls())
library(reproducible) #setting up directories for data management
library(readr)        #Needed to read and merge all the csv's in the camera folder
library(dplyr)        #data wranglin'
library(lubridate)    #datetime manipulation
library(tidyr)        #more data manipulation
library(stringr)      #detecting character strings
library(ggplot2)      #data visualization
library(purrr)        #feline-friendly loops 
library(corrplot)     #correlation tests
library(performance)  #Model Validation
library(ggeffects)    #Model predictions
library(broom.mixed)  #Extracting model coefficients
library(flextable)    #Formatting and writing to worddoc
library(officer)      #Formatting and writing to wordoc


#This just sets up files for inputs (already created, must contain your files), and outputs
#So I am going to something sneaky here, I want to pull in the dataframe that was used for modeling (so I can get variable ranges and whatnot), but thats not the true input directory, so I am going to rename these on the fly 
input_directory<-reproducible::checkPath(file.path(getwd(), "3. Model Selection/outputs"), create = TRUE)
wtd_dets<-read.csv(file.path(input_directory, "final_df.csv"))
#And then go with a new input directory to read in the models
input_directory<-reproducible::checkPath(file.path(getwd(), "4. Models/outputs"), create = TRUE)
output_directory<-reproducible::checkPath(file.path(getwd(), "5. Simulations/outputs"), create = TRUE)



```


```{r}
linear_males<-readRDS(file.path(input_directory, "linear_males.rds"))
summary(linear_males)


#I am going to pull these into a dataframe real quick
lm<-broom.mixed::tidy(linear_males)



#Simulation parameters
n_sites<- 40 #40 sites per array
n_arrays<- 10 #10 arrays 
n_obs<- 2
n<-n_sites*n_arrays*n_obs

#Create some site names
site<-rep(1:n_sites, times = n_arrays, each = n_obs)
array<-rep(LETTERS[1:n_arrays], each = n_sites * n_obs)

df<-data.frame(array, site)

#Define the array level random effect from the model
array_sd<-lm$estimate[lm$effect == "ran_pars" & lm$term == "sd__(Intercept)"]
array_effect<-rep(rnorm(n_arrays, mean = 0, sd = array_sd), each = n_sites*n_obs)

#Still looks good - remember the array effect should be constant through array ID
df<-data.frame(array, site, array_effect)


#Now lets generate some site covariates. Now some of these need to stay the same between years (obs) mind you!
#Lat, linear_index, PC1, PC2 should stay consistent among years. 
lat<-rep(runif(n_sites*n_arrays,  min = min(wtd_dets$lat), max = max(wtd_dets$lat)), each = n_obs)
PC1<-rep(runif(n_sites*n_arrays,  min = min(wtd_dets$PC1), max = max(wtd_dets$PC1)), each = n_obs)
PC2<-rep(runif(n_sites*n_arrays,  min = min(wtd_dets$PC2), max = max(wtd_dets$PC2)), each = n_obs)
linear_index<-rep(runif(n_sites*n_arrays,  min = min(wtd_dets$linear_index), max = max(wtd_dets$linear_index)), each = n_obs)

#mean snow spatial is slightly different, and theoretically it should be different between years (observations), but they should be closely related. So functionally I am going to keep them same for both years of observation for each site. This negates the risk of having a very low value one year, and then randomly a very high value the next year
mean_snow_spatial<-rep(runif(n_sites*n_arrays,  min = min(wtd_dets$mean_snow_spatial), max = max(wtd_dets$mean_snow_spatial)), each = n_obs)


#Check your dataframe to see that its consistent
df<-data.frame(site, array, array_effect, lat, PC1, PC2, mean_snow_spatial)

#And now the other variables, these can vary among years
snow_anomaly<-rep(runif(n_sites*n_arrays*n_obs,  min = min(wtd_dets$snow_anomaly), max = max(wtd_dets$snow_anomaly)))
predator_index<-rep(runif(n_sites*n_arrays*n_obs,  min = min(wtd_dets$predator_index), max = max(wtd_dets$predator_index)))

df<-data.frame(site, array, array_effect, lat, linear_index, PC1, PC2, mean_snow_spatial, snow_anomaly, predator_index)


###################################
#Now define some true parameters
B_intercept<-lm$estimate[lm$term == "(Intercept)"]
B_linear<-lm$estimate[lm$term == "linear_index"]
B_PC1<-lm$estimate[lm$term == "PC1"]
B_PC2<-lm$estimate[lm$term == "PC2"]
B_predator<-lm$estimate[lm$term == "predator_index"]
B_lat<-lm$estimate[lm$term == "lat"]
B_meansnow<-lm$estimate[lm$term == "mean_snow_spatial"]
B_snowanomaly<-lm$estimate[lm$term == "snow_anomaly"]
B_linear_meansnow<-lm$estimate[lm$term == "linear_index:mean_snow_spatial"]
B_linear_snowanomaly<-lm$estimate[lm$term == "linear_index:snow_anomaly"]



#And now we can calculate the linear predictor
linear_predictor<-B_intercept +
  B_linear*df$linear_index+
  B_PC1*df$PC1+
  B_PC2*df$PC2+
  B_predator*df$predator_index+
  B_lat*df$lat+
  B_meansnow*df$mean_snow_spatial+
  B_snowanomaly*df$snow_anomaly+
  B_linear_meansnow * df$linear_index * df$mean_snow_spatial +
  B_linear_snowanomaly * df$linear_index * df$snow_anomaly +
  df$array_effect

#convert linear predictor to probabilities based on logit link funciton
prob<-plogis(linear_predictor)
#The number of "successes" depends on the number of trials and probability of success
#Basing this on four months, four weeks each to be sampled
total_trials<-16
present<-rbinom(n, size = total_trials, prob = prob)
#The number of failures is just the total trials minus total successes
absent<-total_trials - present


#Wrap it into a dataframe
df<-data.frame(site, array, present, absent, array_effect, lat, linear_index, PC1, PC2, mean_snow_spatial, snow_anomaly, predator_index)

#I need something handy to randomly select rows of data to get us down to the real sample size
df<-df[sample(nrow(df), 701),]


#refit the model
linear_males2<-glmmTMB::glmmTMB(cbind(present, absent) ~
                   linear_index+
                   PC1 + PC2 + #Habitat covariates
                   predator_index + #Predator index
                   lat+
                     mean_snow_spatial*linear_index+
                   snow_anomaly*linear_index+
                   (1|array),
                 family = "binomial",
                 data = df)
#Original
summary(linear_males)
#Simulated
summary(linear_males2)

############################################################################################################
#Ok lets wrap this into a function and iterate 100 times
linear_model_simulation<-function(n_arrays = 10,
         n_sites = 40,
         n_obs = 2,
         n = n_arrays*n_sites*n_obs){
  
#Simulation parameters
site<-rep(1:n_sites, times = n_arrays, each = n_obs)
array<-rep(LETTERS[1:n_arrays], each = n_sites * n_obs)
array_sd<-lm$estimate[lm$effect == "ran_pars" & lm$term == "sd__(Intercept)"]
array_effect<-rep(rnorm(n_arrays, mean = 0, sd = array_sd), each = n_sites*n_obs)
#Simulated data - constant per site
lat<-rep(runif(n_sites*n_arrays,  min = min(wtd_dets$lat), max = max(wtd_dets$lat)), each = n_obs)
PC1<-rep(runif(n_sites*n_arrays,  min = min(wtd_dets$PC1), max = max(wtd_dets$PC1)), each = n_obs)
PC2<-rep(runif(n_sites*n_arrays,  min = min(wtd_dets$PC2), max = max(wtd_dets$PC2)), each = n_obs)
linear_index<-rep(runif(n_sites*n_arrays,  min = min(wtd_dets$linear_index), max = max(wtd_dets$linear_index)), each = n_obs)
mean_snow_spatial<-rep(runif(n_sites*n_arrays,  min = min(wtd_dets$mean_snow_spatial), max = max(wtd_dets$mean_snow_spatial)), each = n_obs)
#Simulated data - variable per year
snow_anomaly<-rep(runif(n_sites*n_arrays*n_obs,  min = min(wtd_dets$snow_anomaly), max = max(wtd_dets$snow_anomaly)))
predator_index<-rep(runif(n_sites*n_arrays*n_obs,  min = min(wtd_dets$predator_index), max = max(wtd_dets$predator_index)))
###################################
#Model Parameters
B_intercept<-lm$estimate[lm$term == "(Intercept)"]
B_linear<-lm$estimate[lm$term == "linear_index"]
B_PC1<-lm$estimate[lm$term == "PC1"]
B_PC2<-lm$estimate[lm$term == "PC2"]
B_predator<-lm$estimate[lm$term == "predator_index"]
B_lat<-lm$estimate[lm$term == "lat"]
B_meansnow<-lm$estimate[lm$term == "mean_snow_spatial"]
B_snowanomaly<-lm$estimate[lm$term == "snow_anomaly"]
B_linear_meansnow<-lm$estimate[lm$term == "linear_index:mean_snow_spatial"]
B_linear_snowanomaly<-lm$estimate[lm$term == "linear_index:snow_anomaly"]
#Linear predictor calculations
linear_predictor<-B_intercept +
  B_linear*df$linear_index+
  B_PC1*df$PC1+
  B_PC2*df$PC2+
  B_predator*df$predator_index+
  B_lat*df$lat+
  B_meansnow*df$mean_snow_spatial+
  B_snowanomaly*df$snow_anomaly+
  B_linear_meansnow * df$linear_index * df$mean_snow_spatial +
  B_linear_snowanomaly * df$linear_index * df$snow_anomaly +
  df$array_effect
prob<-plogis(linear_predictor)
total_trials<-16
present<-rbinom(n, size = total_trials, prob = prob)
absent<-total_trials - present

#Wrap it into a dataframe
df<-data.frame(site, array, present, absent, array_effect, lat, linear_index, PC1, PC2, mean_snow_spatial, snow_anomaly, predator_index)

#Randomly reduce to real sample size
df<-df[sample(nrow(df), 701),]

#refit the model
m1<-glmmTMB::glmmTMB(cbind(present, absent) ~
                   linear_index+
                   PC1 + PC2 + #Habitat covariates
                   predator_index + #Predator index
                   lat+
                     mean_snow_spatial*linear_index+
                   snow_anomaly*linear_index+
                   (1|array),
                 family = "binomial",
                 data = df)
  
return(m1)

}
############################################
#Ok lets run that function a few times
set.seed(420)
n_sims<- 100
start_time<-Sys.time()
simple_model_selection_sims<-map(1:n_sims, ~linear_model_simulation())
end_time<-Sys.time()
run_time<-as.numeric(difftime(end_time, start_time), units = "mins")
print(paste("Simulations complete in ", round(run_time), " minutes"))

#Extract model estimates
param_estimates <- map_df(
  simple_model_selection_sims,
  ~ tidy(.x, effects = "fixed", component = "cond"),
  .id = "simulation"
)

#And now for the plots....
ggplot(param_estimates%>%
         filter(term == "PC1"),
       aes(x = estimate)) +
  geom_histogram(bins = 30, color = "black", fill = "grey70")
```
